blocks.content: Eratosthenes calculated the circumference of the Earth using simple geometric observations.

rows: No shadow cast inside a deep well
Definite shadow cast by a vertical pole

items: Eratosthenes is frequently referred to as the 'Father of Geography' in competitive exams.
Remember the two key reference locations in his experiment: Syene (modern-day Aswan) and Alexandria.
Note the mathematical relationship used: an angle of 7.2° represents 1/50th of a 360° sphere.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Eratosthenes was an ancient Greek polymath who provided early scientific evidence for the spherical shape of the Earth.
He measured the Earth's circumference by comparing shadow angles cast by the Sun at noon on the summer solstice in two locations: Syene and Alexandria.
The angular difference of approximately 7.2 degrees between the two cities allowed him to calculate that the distance between them was 1/50th of Earth's total circumference.
This geometric calculation served as one of the earliest and most accurate historical proofs of a spherical Earth.
